details:
TLDR: improve the interaction system by providing tools to the community or building procedural systems

Hey ever since I started to play VRChat actively I've been stunned at how generic the interaction system is coming from being used to what VR games provide.

I understand that it makes sense to have those general grab and trigger interactions so that it fits with any type of content and that it can be utilized with a regular keyboard and mouse/controller.

However I feel like we're not pushing inexperienced creators to use great systems and that even for experienced creators it takes a lot of time to integrate, making it something that end users don't experience as much and therefore get a bad impression of the game.

Bonework's and lone echo's/echoVR's procedural finger placement/animations would make a lot of sense in VRChat.

That being trough making user created hand poses more interactive, or by making something fully procedural:

Here's ready at dawn's Jacob Copenhaver GDC talk on how they did their finger placement system if you don't know what I'm talking about:

https://www.gdcvault.com/play/1024446/It-s-All-in-the

If such a system isn't possible with VRChat's curent IK, having something to set a hand pose when grabbing something would be great alongside some exemple hand poses.

While the controller highlight makes sense to teach new players how to interact with something, I feel like there should either be something that worlds creator's could do to disable them, or let the user overwrite that themselves after a specified amount of grab interaction (could be set to 0 to disable it all together)
title: Interaction update
